title: Pantry Match: recipe suggestions from what's in your pantry
context: Simmer is a consumer recipe app (iOS, Android, web; Rails API on a single Postgres 15 primary with two read replicas) with 2.1M monthly active users, ~78% of them in US time zones. Mission: help home cooks decide what to cook tonight with as little effort as possible. This plan is about to be dispatched to a 4-engineer squad for a 6-week build.
artifact:
# Pantry Match — build plan

Squad: Discovery (3 eng + 1 mobile) | 6 weeks | PM: Discovery PM

## 1. Problem
Churned-user exit survey, Q2 (n = 3,800), top reasons:
1. "Too much setup / typing to get useful suggestions" — 38%
2. "Recipes need ingredients I don't have" — 22%
3. "Same recipes keep showing up" — 15%
Pantry Match targets reason #2: suggest recipes that use what the user already has.

## 2. User experience
- New Pantry tab. Users add items with a form: ingredient (autocomplete over our 9,400-ingredient catalog), quantity, unit, expiry date.
- To keep match quality high, Pantry Match unlocks once a user has entered at least 15 items with expiry dates. Until then the tab shows a progress bar ("7 of 15 items added").
- Users are asked to update quantities after cooking (prompt on the recipe "I made this" screen).
- Home feed gains a "Cook from your pantry" carousel (top 10 matches) once unlocked.

## 3. Matching
- Score = (pantry ingredients used / recipe ingredients) weighted by expiry proximity, with pantry staples (salt, oil, water, pepper) always counted as present.
- Ingredient normalization reuses the existing ingredient_aliases table (e.g. "scallion" = "green onion").

## 4. Compute
- New table pantry_matches(user_id, recipe_id, score, computed_at), top 50 per user.
- PantryMatchJob (Sidekiq, nightly 02:00 UTC): for each user with a pantry, score every recipe in the catalog (340k recipes) in a single SQL statement joining pantry_items x recipe_ingredients on the primary, then upsert the top 50 into pantry_matches.
- Staging run: 12,000 synthetic pantry users completed in 41 minutes.
- Adoption assumption for sizing: 30% of MAU create a pantry within 90 days.

## 5. Notifications
- Optional "use it before it goes bad" push when a pantry item is 2 days from expiry.
- Opt-in only (off by default), max 1 push per user per day, respects existing quiet hours (21:00-08:00 local).

## 6. Timeline
- Weeks 1-2: pantry data model, Pantry tab + item form (iOS/Android/web).
- Week 3: scoring, PantryMatchJob.
- Week 4: home carousel, "I made this" quantity prompt.
- Week 5: notifications, analytics events.
- Week 6: beta to 5% of users, then 100%.

## 7. Success metrics
- 25% of MAU unlock Pantry Match within 60 days.
- +3 pts 30-day retention for users who unlock vs. matched control.

defects.description: Cross-reference §1 vs §2: the #1 churn reason (38%) is too much setup/typing, yet the feature is locked behind manually entering 15 items with quantity, unit and expiry, plus post-cooking quantity updates. The design trades churn reason #2 for amplifying reason #1, so it will likely fail its own unlock and retention metrics.
defects.evidence: Pantry Match unlocks once a user has entered at least 15 items with expiry dates

defects.description: At the 30% adoption assumption (~630k users) the nightly job scores ~2x10^11 user-recipe pairs in single SQL statements on the primary; extrapolating the 12k-user staging run (41 min) linearly gives ~36 hours per nightly run. It also runs at 02:00 UTC, which is US evening dinner-planning peak for a 78%-US user base, so it loads the primary at peak traffic.
defects.evidence: score every recipe in the catalog (340k recipes) in a single SQL statement joining pantry_items x recipe_ingredients on the primary

decoys: Push-notification spam: handled in §5 — opt-in, off by default, 1/day cap, honours quiet hours.
